input:
In this application, a centrifugal pump is used to move caustic solution between two vessels situated at grade. At the duty point, the flow is 34 m3 h-1 against a head of 56 m, and the pump operates with an efficiency of 71%. The shaft power at the duty point works out at 7.3 kW. The motor has been rated 15% above this figure, corresponding to a rating of 8.4 kW. Because both vessels stand at grade, the head is made up entirely of the friction and fitting losses in the line at the duty flow, with no static lift component.

It should be appreciated that the quoted efficiency belongs specifically to the duty point: it represents the ratio of the hydraulic power delivered to the liquid to the shaft power absorbed at that point, and it changes as the flow moves away from the duty point. The motor margin covers the gap between the duty-point shaft power and the motor rating; it is not an allowance for sustained operation far from the duty point, where the absorbed power follows the pump curve. The stated duty is a single point on that curve, and no performance at any other flow is reported.

During the acceptance test, no cavitation was observed. The test was run for 4 h at the duty point only, which means the observation covers that point and that duration, and says nothing about cavitation at other flows, at other suction conditions, or over longer runs, so the reported performance does not extend beyond the tested point.
